title: Age and corotation matched TESS stars retain a CPV deficit at the hot core boundary
abstract: We test whether the reported lack of complex periodic variables (CPVs) in young stars assigned a radiative core requires a fitted corotation-rate curve. From 855 released young TESS rapid rotators, 100 core stars have 283 distinct controls matched on age class, log age, corotation ratio and injection efficiency. The core stars have no CPVs; the controls have 30. Conditional on group counts, equal detected odds give a zero-count probability of 0.0001115 and a one-sided 95% upper core/control odds ratio of 0.2846. A luminosity-based radius gives 0.3240. Fixed-bin comparisons also retain the deficit. Clean-astrometry subsets give weaker evidence and some of the 72 sensitivity settings permit equal odds. The result shows that a fitted x-only extrapolation is not necessary for the boundary signal. It does not separate core status from temperature or mass, identify the material, or estimate intrinsic host rates. Finite matching tolerances, model cores, shared labels and uncertain selection limit inference. We provide original code, attributed parameter code, anonymous sufficient counts, hashes and separate-scratch reproduction.

display.caption: Matched sample size and conditional upper odds bound across corotation tolerances for two radius methods, using up to three controls per core star.

citations.reason: Reuses parameter code and tests the boundary without a fitted rate curve.
Retains the limit that temperature and core effects cannot be separated.
